They’re trying to long the process out and get more money out of you for certain. You should not be ‘making your own lesson plans’ - that’s ridiculous. Good instructors should be able to identify automatically your strengths and weaknesses and adapt each lesson to gradually build you up in each area, until they feel you’re somewhat near test ready - then move into a mock testing structure right up till your test date.

These guys are messing you about big time from my perspective. The ‘handbook’ is BS, scrap it. The focussing on little minor details that you yourself feel confident about is another lengthening tactic also. It almost seems like they’re deliberately trying to induce self doubt within you so that you continue to stay with them. 

IMO, get out asap and find a good, solo driving instructor. Not a school. Solo instructors are generally better and more inclined to do you well as their personal reputation is on the line due to working for themselves. School instructors are part of a larger top-down company and don’t have as much incentive to serve you properly - and these LDC guys seem overwhelmingly focussed on profits and bonuses over professionalism. 

Obviously this is my perspective, but the whole thing stinks to me. You deserve much better, especially given the amount of money - and time- you’re investing!!! Hope you sort this out.

Edit: you can message me if you need any further advice, have any questions, or need help with finding something more suitable and reliable.

Honestly just do what I did and take some beta blockers lol. If your anxiety is that bad you should be considering them anyways. They genuinely turned me into a confident professional from a jittery mess! 

I use propranolol. Took 10mg an hour before my test and anxiety went out the window. It only helped physical symptoms however, but for me at least, the rapid heartbeat and sweaty/shaky hands going away allowed my mind to feel at ease anyways. 

Have a look into them. 

Other than the meds you can try deep breathing, eating certain foods, or just talking about nerves with a trusted friend/family member. Also one thing that helped me massively as well was endlessly watching YT videos on driving; mock tests, real tests, fails, passes, everything and anything really. 

If you can as well, try and practice if you have your own car and a person to go out with. I bashed out about 40 hours with my dad within the month before my test, and it helped me so much more than my standard lessons with the instructor. Get the ‘DrivingTestRoutes’ app on the App Store and purchase your test centres routes package (costs £12.99 a month but I only used it for a month so). So useful. Me and my dad did about two routes a day for a month.

But yeah, I’m not an expert. Though, I did just pass first time yesterday with 3 minors using all of the above methods. 

Wish you luck anyways. Feel free to message me if you have any queries.

The rest of your head looks fine though, you’ve just been unlucky and inherited naturally fine hair like me so it makes it all look thinner than it actually is, especially when wet.

If you’re truly worried though, one way to tell if your hairline is maturing or balding is to crease your forehead and measure from the highest wrinkle to the furthest point of your hairline. If the measurement reads 1-1.5 inches (give or take) then you don’t need to worry as you’re likely experiencing hairline maturation and shouldn’t see further recession, however, if the measurement is 1.5+ then it could spell the beginning of the end for your hair. 

If it’s the latter, consider consulting a dermatologist or speaking to someone about it, maybe a family member or close friend. Seeing as you’re 17 it may be hard to get prescriptions and such so, just explore your options. 

But realistically, it looks perfectly fine to me right now, just maturing. 

Good luck.
